    33	\section{Setup and motivation}
    34	\label{sec:pic0_setup}
    35	
    36	Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper
    37	geometrically integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) of genus \(g = g(C)\)
    38	(\cref{def:genus}). By
    39	\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and \cref{thm:pic_is_group_scheme}, the
    40	\'etale-sheafified relative Picard functor of \(C/k\) is represented by
    41	the \(k\)-group scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\) (\cref{def:pic_scheme}), which is
    42	separated, locally of finite type over \(k\), and a disjoint union of
    43	open quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes. The disjoint-union structure of
    44	\(\Pic_{C/k}\) stratifies its \(T\)-points by the Hilbert polynomial of the
    45	representing invertible sheaf relative to a fixed polarisation, and on
    46	the geometric points of the curve this stratification reduces to the
    47	degree of a line bundle.

    49	The identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) singled out by Kleiman is the open
    50	and closed subgroup scheme consisting of the connected component of
    51	\(\Pic_{C/k}\) containing the trivial line bundle. It is the locus of
    52	degree-zero classes, and on a smooth proper curve it is itself an
    53	abelian variety of dimension \(g\) --- the Jacobian variety of \(C\). This
    54	chapter packages those four statements as the A.3 specification.
